title: Bump version to 0.2.4
description:
v0.2.3 predates the LICENSE and COPYRIGHT files added in #3, so its tagged release tarball has no license text. conda-forge requires the tarball to contain the license, so this release exists purely to give conda-forge staged-recipes a tarball it can package - no code changes.

This unblocks the quarto-feedstock bump to Quarto 1.10.18, which depends on that staged-recipes PR.

title: Add license files and crate metadata (unblocks conda-forge packaging)
description:
## Why

I'm working on the conda-forge packaging of `typst-gather` so that Quarto 1.10 can depend on it at runtime. As of v0.2.3 the crate can't be packaged.

conda-forge requires every recipe to declare **both** a license identifier (`about.license`) and to ship the actual license text (`about.license_file`). A recipe cannot pass staged-recipes review without both. At v0.2.3 this repo has neither:

- there is no `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSE.txt` or `COPYING` file anywhere in the repo root
- `Cargo.toml`'s `[package]` block has `name`, `version`, `edition`, `repository` and `rust-version`, but no `license`

Without the package, Quarto falls back to staging every Typst package and warns on each render, and `quarto call typst-gather` fails outright.

## What this changes

- **`LICENSE`** — full MIT text, `Copyright (c) 2026 Posit Software, PBC`. The text is byte-identical to quarto-cli's `COPYING.md` apart from the copyright year, so it matches the license already used across the Quarto project.
- **`COPYRIGHT`** — mirrors quarto-cli's `COPYRIGHT` layout (project name, copyright line, MIT text, source URL). I dropped quarto-cli's "with the exceptions noted below" clause since this repo vendors no third-party source, and added a short paragraph noting that the linked Typst components (`typst-kit`, `typst-syntax`) are Apache-2.0.
- **`Cargo.toml` `[package]`** — adds `license = "MIT"`, plus `description` and `readme = "README.md"`, which were also empty and which crates.io requires to publish:

```diff
 [package]
 name = "typst-gather"
 version = "0.2.3"
 edition = "2021"
+description = "Gather Typst packages locally for offline/hermetic builds."
+license = "MIT"
+readme = "README.md"
 repository = "https://github.com/quarto-dev/typst-gather"
 rust-version = "1.81"
```

`description` is taken verbatim from the README's one-line summary. I left `homepage` out deliberately — with no site distinct from the repo it would only duplicate `repository`.

Copyright years are `2026`, matching this repo's own commit history (first commit 2026-03-06) rather than quarto-cli's wider `2020-2024` range. Happy to change that to a range if you'd prefer consistency with quarto-cli's line.

## Notes for review

- **`Cargo.lock` is unchanged.** These are metadata-only manifest keys and don't perturb the lockfile, so the committed lockfile stays valid — which matters because conda-forge builds with `--locked`.
- Verified with `cargo verify-project` (`{"success":"true"}`) and `cargo metadata`, which resolves `license = MIT`, `description` and `readme` as intended.
- MIT for this crate is compatible with the Apache-2.0 Typst dependencies; Apache-2.0 is permissive, and the feedstock bundles the vendored deps' notices through its own `license_file` list rather than through this crate's `license` field.
- Not touched, to keep the diff minimal: `keywords`, `categories` and `authors` are also absent from `[package]`. None of them block conda-forge or `cargo publish`. Glad to add them here if you'd rather land all the crates.io metadata at once.

## A tagged release is needed afterwards

Merging this is necessary but not sufficient. A conda-forge feedstock points at a **versioned source tarball with a stable sha256**, so it needs a new tag containing these files — **v0.2.4** (or later) — rather than a moving branch ref. Tarballs generated from a branch aren't checksum-stable and staged-recipes won't accept them.

So the sequence is: merge this → tag and release v0.2.4 → I submit the feedstock to staged-recipes pointing at that tag. If you'd like the release to carry anything else, that's a good moment to batch it in.

title: Pin Linux release runner to ubuntu-22.04, bump to 0.2.3
description:
## Summary

- Pin the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` release jobs to `ubuntu-22.04` (was `ubuntu-latest`).
- Bump version to `0.2.3`.

## Why

Reported in [quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14445](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/14445): `typst-gather` v0.2.2 binaries fail on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, and RHEL 9 with:

```
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
```

This breaks Quarto 1.10's Typst pipeline, including in Quarto's own first-party container image (`ghcr.io/quarto-dev/quarto:1.10.3`, based on Ubuntu 22.04).

## Root cause

`objdump -T` on the v0.2.2 release artefacts (both x64 and arm64) shows a single symbol holding the GLIBC floor at 2.38: `__isoc23_strtol`. Every other libc symbol is `<= 2.34`.

All three call sites land inside vendored OpenSSL — two in DRBG seed-source code (`seed_src_*`) and one in X.509 verification (`verify_chain` neighbourhood). No other dep contributes.

`ubuntu-latest` now resolves to Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39). Starting in glibc 2.38, the headers redirect `strtol` (and friends) to `__isoc23_strtol` for C23 conformance. OpenSSL's static archive picks up that redirect at compile time and bakes the symbol into our binary.

v0.1.x was unaffected because it had no `vendored-openssl` feature — `openssl-sys` dynamic-linked to the system libssl, so the strtol call resolved at the user's runtime against the user's libc. The static-vendor switch landed in 7f33d8c (March 2026) to fix aarch64 cross-compile linking; that's when the floor appeared. The runner image bump (22 -> 24) had to happen too, which is why this only bit Quarto 1.10.

## The fix

Pin the Linux release matrix entries to `ubuntu-22.04`. That image ships glibc 2.35, whose headers do not define the C23 strtol redirect macros, so OpenSSL compiles plain `strtol` calls. The binary's floor drops to glibc 2.34 (the next-highest symbol used), restoring compatibility with the distros Quarto documents.

`ubuntu-22.04` runners are supported until June 2027. We should plan a more durable answer (`cargo-zigbuild` with a pinned glibc target, or a manylinux-style container build) before the runner is retired. Filed as a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release` clean locally
- [x] `cargo test --release` — 41 passed, 5 ignored (network), 0 failed
- [x] Smoke-tested `typst-gather analyze` end-to-end on a sample config + `.typ` file with `@preview` imports
- [ ] CI green on this PR (Linux/macOS/Windows)
- [ ] After merge + tag, verify release artefact `objdump -T | grep GLIBC_2.38` returns nothing
- [ ] After merge + tag, smoke-test the new binary inside `ghcr.io/quarto-dev/quarto:1.10.3` (Ubuntu 22.04)
